verdicts.reason: A and B look the same: the headline and tagline lockup sits about 30px right of the banner's centre and hugs the top, leaving a dead band of roughly 35px below. The original is centred on both axes, so this centring is lost, but the type is readable and on brand.

A pushes the lockup about 50px left of centre and B pushes it about 50px right. Both are stuck to the top with empty space below, and the letter-spaced tagline is very small at banner size. Both have the same flaws with the offset mirrored, so neither is clearly better.

A shrinks the headline further and is about 70px left of centre, and its tagline is close to illegible. B is just as top-heavy and about 50px left of centre, but its headline and tagline are slightly larger and easier to read.

A has the largest, most legible headline and tagline, about 33px left of centre, though it is still top-aligned with dead space below. B shifts the lockup about 70px right of centre, leaving a large empty left half, and shrinks the tagline into barely readable micro-type.
